claims.text: Adding a controlled amount of a precipitate-forming element such as Ti to Co-free FeNiCrMn can induce precipitation strengthening.
Ti is a suitable precipitate-forming addition for FeNiCrMn.
Adding Ti to FeNiCrMn will produce precipitates such as TiC or TiN.
The resulting precipitates will hinder dislocation movement.
Precipitation strengthening will enhance the strength of the alloy.
Precipitation strengthening will enhance strength without significantly compromising ductility.
The modification will improve the strength-ductility balance relative to unmodified Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The improved strength-ductility balance will occur under dynamic loading.
The hypothesis is valid from room temperature to 600 K.
The hypothesis is valid at strain rates from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
The relevant initial material may be either as-cast or solution-treated Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The optimal amount of precipitate-forming addition is uncertain.
Interactions between the precipitates and other microstructural features may affect the response.
The effect of precipitation strengthening on fatigue behavior is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The loading regime is described as dynamic, but the stated lower strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 is conventionally quasi-static rather than dynamic.

The intervention specifies only addition of a precipitate-forming element such as Ti, whereas the proposed TiC or TiN mediators also require available carbon or nitrogen; their source or addition is not specified.
